newsitem.title: GERMANY: German insolvencies climb to record high in 1996.
newsitem.headline: German insolvencies climb to record high in 1996.

text.p: The number of insolvencies in Germany reached a record high in 1996 for the fourth year in a row, climbing 9.3 percent to 31,471, the German Federal Statistics Office said on Wednesday.
Insolvencies in east Germany posted the highest climb, up 18.7 percent to 8,393. Some 7,419 of those were companies.
In west Germany, the number of insolvencies last year climbed 6.3 percent to 23,078, 18,111 of those being companies.
The picture brightened somewhat in December, however, with the number of insolvencies in all of Germany declining 5.8 percent to 2,539.
